title: U.S. House · Texas's 27th Congressional District
area: Coastal South Texas, including Victoria and the Corpus Christi area.

context.text: Texas redrew its congressional district boundaries in August 2025 ahead of the 2026 elections, a mid-decade redistricting.

In the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, Tanya Lloyd defeated Eustaquio Castro-Mendoza and Wayne Raasch. Raasch subsequently ran as a write-in independent candidate in the general election. Incumbent Michael Cloud defeated Chris Hatley in the Republican primary.

summary.text: Michael Cloud is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Texas's 27th District. A former Victoria County Republican Party chairman, church media director and small-business owner, he first won the seat in a June 2018 special election and has been re-elected since. He serves on the Appropriations and Oversight committees and is seeking another term.

background.text: Born in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and graduated from Miamisburg High School in Ohio.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Oral Roberts University.

Worked as media and communications director at Faith Family Church in Victoria, Texas, and owned Bright Ideas Media, according to Ballotpedia. His official biography describes him as a small business owner and a longtime District 27 resident.
Served on the Texas State Executive Republican Committee and as chairman of the Victoria County Republican Party.
Won a special election on June 30, 2018, for the 27th District seat, succeeding Rep. Blake Farenthold, and took office July 10, 2018. He won a full term in November 2018 with 60.3% of the vote.

Serves on the House Appropriations Committee, where Ballotpedia lists him as vice chair of the Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Subcommittee, and on the Oversight and Government Reform Committee.
Defeated Chris Hatley in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary to advance to the November general election.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and the House Committee on Appropriations, including as Vice Chair of its Energy and Water Development subcommittee, in the 119th Congress.

summary.text: Tanya Lloyd is a kindergarten teacher who says she has spent about two decades in public schools after earlier work in car dealerships, accounting and real estate. She won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 63.1% of the vote and describes her platform as rural hospitals, childcare, public school funding and a $17 minimum wage.

background.text: Graduated from Lockhart High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Texas State University in 2006, according to Ballotpedia.
In her Candidate Connection survey, says she worked in car dealerships, accounting and real estate before becoming a mother, and earned her teaching degree at age 33.

Has worked as a public school teacher; in her survey she describes herself as a kindergarten teacher with about two decades in public schools. Her campaign materials describe her as a Texas AFT member.
Has served on school district advisory and bond oversight committees in her community, according to her campaign materials as reproduced by Ballotpedia.
Describes herself as a mom, lifelong Texan and progressive, running on what she calls an American Rural Revival, and says she takes no corporate PAC money.
Defeated Eustaquio Castro-Mendoza and Wayne Raasch in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, 63.1% to 29.4% and 7.5%.

priorities.text: In her 2026 Ballotpedia survey, said her priorities are lowering costs for working families, fully funding public education, strengthening rural healthcare access, and investing in rural infrastructure such as broadband and water systems.

positions.summary: Says she would oppose voucher programs that divert public dollars to private interests, and would fight to fully fund public schools.
positions.quote: oppose voucher programs that divert public dollars to private interests

positions.summary: In a candidate questionnaire she says she supports moving toward a universal system like Medicare for All.
positions.quote: I support moving toward a universal system like Medicare for All

positions.summary: In her Ballotpedia survey she lists protecting reproductive rights, with the government not coming between women and their doctors, among her key messages.
positions.quote: Standing up for reproductive rights: ensuring the government doesn't get between women and their doctors.

positions.summary: In a candidate questionnaire she says she supports raising the minimum wage and indexing it to inflation, with small-business tax relief and a phase-in.
positions.quote: I support raising the minimum wage (and indexing it to inflation) to ensure that any Texan working a full-time job can actually afford to live in the community where they work.

positions.summary: In a candidate questionnaire she says she supports progressive taxation and making multinational corporations pay their fair share.
positions.quote: By closing loopholes used by the ultra-wealthy and ensuring multinational corporations pay their fair share, we can reduce the tax burden on middle-class families and small business owners.

candidates.name: Wayne Raasch
candidates.ballotNote: Lost the Democratic primary, then filed as a write-in independent candidate for the general election

summary.text: Wayne Raasch is running as a write-in independent candidate after receiving 7.5% in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary for this seat. Ballotpedia lists him as a repeat Democratic primary candidate for Texas offices since 2016.

background.text: Ran in the 2016 Democratic primary for Texas's 27th District, which Roy Barrera won.
Ran in the March 1, 2022 Democratic primary for Texas State Board of Education District 2, receiving 5.4% of the vote.
Lost the March 5, 2024 Democratic primary for Texas's 22nd District, receiving 18.3% of the vote.
Received 7.5% in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary for the 27th District, then filed as a write-in independent for the general election.
